draft.title: Protagonist and antagonist
card: the main character the story follows. The reader usually sees events through their goals, choices and struggles.
the person or force that works against the protagonist and creates conflict. It can be a rival, a villain, a storm or even a society's rules.
The protagonist is the one the story follows, not always the one who is good or wins. Some protagonists make poor choices, and some antagonists are not evil.
Without an antagonist there would be no conflict, so the protagonist would have nothing to push against and the plot would have little to drive it.
draft.remember: The protagonist is the one the story follows. The antagonist is whatever works against them.

a.q: What is the role of the antagonist in a story?
opts: To work against the protagonist and create conflict
To follow the main character and tell the story
To guide the protagonist with wise advice
To stay the same from the start to the end
a.why: The antagonist is the person or force that opposes the protagonist, and this creates conflict. The second option describes the protagonist, which is the tempting mix-up.
a.clue: Think about who or what gets in the main character's way.

b.q: In a story, Tariq is lost in a bushfire and fights to reach his family. The story follows only him. Who or what is the antagonist?
opts: The bushfire, because it works against Tariq
Tariq, because the story follows him
Tariq's family, because he wants to reach them
There is none, because no villain appears
b.why: The bushfire is a force that works against Tariq and creates the conflict, so it is the antagonist. A villain is not needed: an antagonist can be a force of nature.
b.clue: An antagonist does not have to be a person.

a.best: To work against the protagonist and create conflict

b.best: The bushfire, because it works against Tariq
